rated_messages.input_message: To keep on track, small changes can really help. For example, keep a list of quit reasons where you used to keep cigarettes, rearrange your living space, or grab some extra pens to fiddle with to keep your hands busy.
Instead of smoking, take 10 deep, slow breaths and count them. Pay attention to what your breathing feels like. If you lose count, that's okay, just start over at 1 until you get to 10.

Read this rule out loud (if you can): IF someone offers me a cigarette THEN I will say 'no thanks, I don't want one.' Reading out if/then rules has been shown to help people stick with their decisions.
If you miss doing something with your hands, try turning a coin or pen over and over with your fingers.

Think of urges as loud construction noises. Sometimes there's nothing you can do except agree that it's annoying. If you fight it, you feel more irritated, right? Let your urge be there until it passes on its own.
Seeing other people smoke is a predictable and unavoidable trigger. Take 5 slow, deep breaths and remind yourself that the urge will pass and that you do not need to smoke.
Stress is temporary. It comes and goes like passing clouds in the sky. When stress demands you to light up, remember you can let it pass by without smoking.
You don’t need to get rid of or change your thoughts about smoking—just let them pass by like a cloud in the sky.
Ask yourself, "What do I need right now? Is it really a smoke, or is there something else I need? How can I best take care of myself right now?"
Just because other people are smoking, doesn't mean you have to. Practice allowing this urge to be present for 5 minutes. When it passes, give yourself credit.
